title: Expondo — The DOer
desc: A company value turned into a character people can say

blocks.title: Expondo — The DOer
blocks.lede: Turn a company value into something people can actually say.

items.label: Role
items.value: Concept, naming, character design, internal communication, animation

items.label: Scope
items.value: Concept, naming, character system, posters, print, animation

items.statement: The values sounded fine. Nobody owned them.
body: Ambition. Collaboration. Accountability. The usual corporate vocabulary.
The problem wasn’t that they were wrong. They were just too generic to become part of everyday conversation.

items.statement: Instead of describing a value, I gave people an attitude: DO.
body: Then I turned it into a character. The existing Expondo “DO” mark became the starting point for a mascot that could move, react and communicate rather than simply sit on a poster.

blocks.text: A value nobody can say out loud isn’t much of a value.

body: The DOer was taken from rough pencil sketches through to final animation, then extended into workplace posters, print collateral and internal communication.
It stayed grounded in the existing Expondo identity: playful enough to be memorable, but never detached from a company built around real tools and real work.
An abstract list of values became one word people could actually use. The DOer became a recognisable internal voice for announcements, onboarding, presentations and updates.
The useful part of the project wasn’t making a mascot. It was making the culture easier to recognise.
